title: feat(app-shell): the Studio landing lists recent packages, stored by identity and labelled at render (objectui#11863, Q3)
body:
Part of #11863 (Q3)

Clause-②: yes. This widens the published `RecentItemType` union of `@object-ui/app-shell` by one member, `'package'`, so `RecentNamedItem` and `RecentItem` carry it too. A host's exhaustive `switch` or `Record` over the union must handle it. The published `useRecentItemLabel` also takes one new optional argument, `{ packages }`. No export is added or removed. The changeset is `minor` for `@object-ui/app-shell`.

This covers only Q3 of objectstack-ai/objectui#11863, per the retriage ruling (Q3 → A): recent packages on the Studio landing. Q1 (the `/studio` header) and Q2 (search) follow in later rounds, so #11863 remains open. Recent objects and flows wait for a later card. objectstack-ai/objectui#11912 is not addressed here.

## What changed

- **Store** (`RecentItemsProvider.tsx`): `RecentItemType` gains `'package'`, a `RecentNamedItem` kind. A package entry is stored by identity, in the objectui#11678 shape: `id` is `package:PKG`, `name` is the package id, and `href` is the bare `/studio/PKG` route, which opens the Data pillar. It stores no display text. If a caller hands in a `label`, the reader drops it.
- **Producer** (`StudioRoute.tsx`, the route owner): the `:packageId/:tab` leg is now `StudioPackageBuilder`, which records the visit and then renders the builder exactly as before. It sits behind the entry gate, so a refused principal records nothing. It is keyed on the package, not the pillar, so moving between one package's pillars changes nothing and writes nothing. The package-less scope `~org` is skipped. `StudioLanding`'s header is untouched (it belongs to Q1).
- **Label** (`useRecentItemLabel`): a new `package` case returns the `name` of the package's row in the `packages` list the caller hands in. With no row, or no list, it shows the machine name. That is what objectui#11678 draws for a missing object, page or report.
- **Landing** (`BuilderLanding.tsx`): a "Recently viewed" row (the existing `engine.home.recent` key) sits above the package cards. It shows the last three package entries, labelled from the package list the page already loads, and each links to its `/studio/PKG` route. It appears only once that list has answered, so no entry is drawn as its id while the list loads, and it is absent when there are none. The existing cards are unchanged.
- **i18n**: one `home.recentApps.itemType.package` row in each of the ten packs. `pnpm check:i18n-keys` checks this key family against the union exactly.

## H2: every consumer of the recent list, and what it does with a `package` entry

| Consumer | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Home's Recently Accessed (`HomePage`, then `HomeRail.HomeContinue`) | allow-list: object, dashboard, page, record | unchanged: the package entry is left out. Home loads no package list, and packages are listed on the Studio landing. |
| `RecentApps` (exported, not mounted in this tree) | draws what its caller passes | unchanged: the caller chooses the kinds (Home filters before it renders). |
| App sidebar Recent group (`UnifiedSidebar`) | drew every kind | **leaves package entries out.** It loads no package list, and `GET /api/v1/packages` is a Studio read, so drawing the entry could only show the id. |
| Command palette recent group | `type === 'record'` only | unchanged: left out |
| metadata-admin app home (`StudioHomePage`) | drew every kind, through an exhaustive `Record` over the type | **leaves package entries out.** Its own package list (`buildPackageScopeOptions`) holds writable bases only, so a read-only package would draw as its id. |
| `useRecentItemLabel` | its default branch returned `item.label` | new `package` case (above) |
| `BuilderLanding` | none | the new consumer; it labels from its list |

No surface draws a live package as its raw id.

## Hypotheses, measured

- **H1 holds.** I reverse-verified with every non-test source file restored to the base `1473757bf` and the new tests run over it. With the builder mounted at `/studio/com.acme.crm/data`, the real `RecentItemsProvider` held `[]` (`expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`). After the change, the same visit stores exactly one entry: `{"id":"package:com.acme.crm","type":"package","name":"com.acme.crm","href":"/studio/com.acme.crm","visitedAt":…}`. It has no `label`, and the persisted copy equals it. In the browser (below), two visits and one pillar switch inside the first package left exactly two entries, each in that shape.
- **H2:** the table above.
- **H3 holds.** A renamed package draws its new name (unit test, and in the browser `Acme CRM` became `Acme Sales`). A package the list no longer has draws its id, `com.example.showcase`, following the missing-object precedent rather than a new rule. A package's manifest `name` is a plain string in the spec (`ManifestSchema.name` is `z.ZodString`), so it has no per-language form. On the landing, a language switch can only change the row's heading, the existing `engine.home.recent` key. I did not pin a language switch: the name has nothing to switch.
- **H4 holds.** In Chromium at 1440×900, against a mocked API and my own vite dev server from this worktree at `c55b3f62b` (the later commit touches neither the landing nor the route), with three packages (two writable, one read-only):
  - The landing ends at y=630 with no recent package, and at y=735 with two. The rest of the page stays as it was, and the viewport still holds the whole page.
  - The recent links read `Showcase | com.example.showcase` and `Acme CRM | com.acme.crm` (newest first), and the first one opened `/studio/com.example.showcase/data`.
  - There were no page errors.
  - The first dev's earlier y=480 reading came from a different package set, so I compared the two states with the same fixture.

## Tests

All readings are at head `c39af0271` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`) unless a line names another commit. Commands were run from the worktree root, through the shared verify lock.

- New: `StudioRoute.recentPackage-11863.test.tsx` (the real `studioRoutes` inside the real store), `BuilderLanding.recentPackages-11863.test.tsx`, `UnifiedSidebar.recentPackage-11863.test.tsx` and `StudioHomePage.recentPackage-11863.test.tsx`. New cases were also added to `useRecentItemLabel.test.tsx` and `RecentItemsProvider.test.tsx`.
- Reverse verification, run from the committed change `c55b3f62b` with all six source files at the base content. The swap was checked on disk by blob hashes, and a trap restored from `HEAD`, proven by blob hashes and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Result across the six files: `Tests 17 failed | 22 passed (39)`. The 22 that stayed green are the 14 pre-existing provider cases, the 4 pre-existing resolver cases, and 4 negative controls: the landing with no recent package, the sidebar control, and the two route cases that must record nothing. Direction: every case that asserts the new behaviour went red.
- Test union at `c39af0271`:
  - every test that imports `RecentItemsProvider`, `useRecentItems`, `useTrackRouteAsRecent`, `useRecentItemLabel`, `BuilderLanding`, `StudioRoute`, `UnifiedSidebar` or `StudioHomePage` (68 files, from `git grep -l`): `Test Files 68 passed (68)` · `Tests 616 passed (616)`;
  - `scripts/__tests__/`: `Test Files 179 passed | 2 skipped (181)` · `Tests 5452 passed | 2 skipped (5454)`;
  - `packages/i18n/` at `c55b3f62b`: `Test Files 82 passed (82)` · `Tests 1316 passed | 13 skipped (1329)`. The later commit touches no i18n file.
- **Type-check**, at `c39af0271` and after building the console's dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...'`, `Tasks: 34 successful, 34 total`), via `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell --filter @object-ui/console --filter @object-ui/i18n run type-check`. Each script name was echoed (`packages/i18n type-check$`, `packages/app-shell type-check$`, `apps/console type-check$`) and the exit was 0. The first build, at `c55b3f62b`, failed with TS2741 in `StudioHomePage.tsx`: `Exclude` over the `RecentItem` union removes no arm, so the icon map still needed a `package` key. `c39af0271` narrows on the type member instead.
- **Gates** at `c39af0271`, all exit 0:
  - `pnpm check:i18n-keys`: `116 member key(s) checked exactly`, with the `home.recentApps.itemType.` family read against `RecentItemType`;
  - `check:i18n-drift`: `No en value changed in this range.`;
  - `check:i18n-dead-keys`, report-only: the new key sits under the live `home.recentApps.itemType.` head;
  - `check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`;
  - `check:control-bytes`: OK;
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: `22 source file(s) of 3 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`;
  - `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`: no findings;
  - `check:skill-examples`: `Every marked skill example holds up against the built types.`
- **`check:readme-exports`**: exit 1, from an unmet precondition only. 8 bindings were unjudged because `@object-ui/cli` and `@object-ui/plugin-ai` are not in the console closure, so they were not built. All 8 are in `packages/cli/README.md` and `packages/plugin-ai/README.md`, which this diff does not touch. Of the 579 self-bindings, 571 were judged real, 0 fabricated and 0 wrong-path. Every `@object-ui/app-shell` (22) and `@object-ui/i18n` (29) README binding is real, `useRecentItems` and `useRecentItemLabel` included.
- **Bundle** (eager closure): I ran two `vite build`s of the console on the same tree and dependency builds. The second had every changed source file and the ten packs at the base content (restored from `HEAD` by trap, proven by blob hashes). Readings from `pnpm check:eager-closure`:
  - before: `3311.5 KB gzipped` (3390969 B);
  - after: `3311.6 KB gzipped` (3391056 B), against a budget of `3312.0 KB`, headroom `0.4 KB`;
  - delta: +87 B gzipped (+348 B raw). Rolldown folded the small `useRecentItemLabel` chunk into `nav-selection`, now that `BuilderLanding` imports it too.

  The PR's own Bundle Analysis verdict: NOT MEASURED, because it had not posted when this was written.
- **Lint**, narrowed: `eslint --format json` over the 22 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files (the count is from its JSON output) gave 0 errors. Each file's warning count equals the count for its base content, linted through stdin under the same path. The config applies to `**/*.{ts,tsx}` and is not type-aware (`eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- Not run: a reverse check of `check:i18n-keys` with the new en row removed. The session's safety classifier refused the scripted edit, so it is NOT MEASURED.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs (AGENTS.md #2), outside the claimed surface, so not edited.** `packages/app-shell/README.md` ("A recent object, dashboard, page or report entry stores its identity only…") and `content/docs/guide/user-state-persistence.md` ("An object, dashboard, page or report entry in the recent list is stored as its `type` and `name`…") do not yet name the package kind. Suggested sentence for both: "A Studio package entry (`type: 'package'`) is stored the same way; label it with `useRecentItemLabel({ packages })`, passing the package list you loaded, or leave it out where you have no list." I left this for the seat to add to the claim or to carry.
- `RecentApps` (exported, not mounted in this tree) draws whatever list its caller passes and labels it with `useRecentItemLabel()` and no package list. A host that hands it an unfiltered list would see a package entry drawn as its id. No caller in this tree does that: Home filters first. Carrier: none. Noted here, not filed.
